chapter: Black and Tan and Kansas City nightlife
title: The Sunset Club on Twelfth Street, Piney Brown and the radio breakfast show
summary: At Piney Brown's Sunset Club, Turner did a five a.m. radio breakfast show heard as far as New York.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I met Pete when I was a young man but we went... John Hammond, after we moved to Twelfth Street... We move out on Twelfth Street, a joint called the Sunset Club, and they had a fellow runnin' it called Piney Brown.
And later on, when I went to New York City...I'm jumpin' ahead of myself.

I made a number about Piney Brown 'cause I used to work for him all the time, and we worked on...we worked on Twelfth Street-- Twelfth and Highland--to a nightclub called the Sunset Club. Across the street they had a club called the Lone Star. Some I-talians run that. Colored people run the joint where I worked at. So I, uh...we used to do shows in the mornin'--five o'clock in the mornin'. They had a radio station they had built, and they didn't have enough talent to go around early in the mornin', so they got the idea of comin' down to the nightclub, and we'd have a breakfast show five o'clock in the mornin', and we'd go on the air. It reached way up in New York City that time o' mornin'...all around. So, we had a bunch of good boys playin' for us. Some of 'em played with Count Basie, some played with Duke Ellington, and they worked
with us on the bandstand. They's come and sit in. They didn't all work at the same place. We worked in Kansas City at different joints.
